I give up. I can't produce a proof of this statement in the time and tools available, and I don't think a short proof exists.

The statement is `(∀ f, Continuous f → P f → f = 0) ↔ False`, so I would need to show that some continuous, nonzero `f` on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)` has zero integral over every unit sphere. That requires an explicit non-trivial construction. I don't have one, and I'm not confident it exists in the form needed. The Putnam 2019 A4 answer is one I don't recall with certainty, so I can't even tell which direction the formal `False` is meant to encode.

The other direction, proving every such `f` is zero, would need a uniqueness theorem for unit-sphere mean transforms in Lean/Mathlib. That is also far beyond what I can build here.
